judged_text: In Google `deleteEvent` (`packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` ~lines 312-315), the same dead-code fallback yields `calendarId: undefined` when `externalCalendarId` is missing, so cancelled bookings leave orphaned events on users' real Google calendars, and depending on how `apiDeletes` is awaited a rejected promise may fail the whole cancel flow.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `deleteEvent` now computes `calendarId` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is missing/undefined, the `find` predicate compares against `undefined`, so it will almost always return `undefined` and the code will fall back (via later defaulting) to deleting from `primary` rather than the event’s actual destination calendar. Previously it used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` directly, so this change can leave events orphaned on non-primary calendars when references don’t carry `externalCalendarId`.
